title: Railfold Workbench — Strata Switcher & Route Harmonization
creator: Anika Patel
description:
Goal: Reduce cognitive load and token-cost hunting in the Console by compressing lateral navigation into a single adaptive rail (the 'Railfold') that surfaces workspace strata (high-level org, workspace, project) and harmonizes routing so deep links and rollouts map predictably across tiers.

Scope:
- Replace current multi-rail/sidebar patterns with a single collapsible Railfold that supports three strata levels and pinned quick routes.
- Add a lightweight strata toggle (Strata Switcher) to move between org/workspace/project contexts without leaving the current canvas state where possible.
- Standardize route semantics for rollouts and cost dashboards so A/B and canary routes preserve workspace context.
- Provide a progressive reveal mode for mobile/compact widths and a dense mode for high-FTE accounts.

Key design constraints and tradeoffs:
- Must not increase click-depth for common tasks (deploy, model route, cost drilldowns). Tradeoff: we hide some low-frequency links behind the More menu to keep primary actions visible.
- Need to preserve keyboard/navigation accessibility for power users; the rail must support arrow, home/end, and type-to-jump.
- Performance: structure should avoid additional client-side routing hops during simple context switches (prefer stateful overlay + shallow route fragment).
- Rollout compatibility: the new routing schema must be backwards-compatible with existing deep links for the first stage; later we will migrate links with a short-lived redirect shim.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Prototype validated in 3 moderated usability sessions with PMs/SEs showing reduced time-to-switch by at least 20%.
2) New route mapping preserves previous deep-link paths (legacy links redirect with no loss of context).
3) Accessibility checks: all railfold elements reach 4.5:1 contrast; keyboard nav passes internal AX audit.
4) Design token/specs and redlines published in Figma + Confluence; dev handoff includes interaction spec and edge-case matrix.

Deliverables:
- High-fidelity Figma prototype that demonstrates dense, normal, and compact breakpoints.
- Interaction spec doc: route mapping table, state preservation rules, keyboard behavior.
- Usability notes and prioritized tweaks.

Risk & open questions:
- How will customer-level feature flags (Dedicated vs Hosted customers) influence visible strata? (Need PM input)
- Small accounts may prefer a simplified rail; should we auto-collapse by account size or offer a user preference?
- Backend routing changes required: ENG to confirm feasibility of preserving KV cache/state across shallow route fragments.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Design prototype -> 2) Engineering spike to validate shallow route fragment and redirect shim -> 3) Internal pilot with Platform team -> 4) Gradual rollout behind feature flag + telemetry.

Notes: Avoid reusing patterns that caused latency spikes in prior experiments (see ENG-1934). Focus on observable metrics (time-to-switch, click-depth, route-mismatch rate).
